content: Hemophilia A and B are genetic disorders that result in either a reduced or completely absent level of clotting factor VIII or IX, respectively. In severe cases, the levels of these factors are less than 0.01 international units (IU) per milliliter. A major complication in the treatment of hemophilia is the development of inhibitors, which are antibodies that neutralize the effectiveness of replacement therapy. The presence of these inhibitors makes it extremely challenging to manage bleeding episodes. Individuals with inhibitors face significantly higher risks of both morbidity and mortality, and their treatment is associated with substantial costs. Rituximab, a monoclonal antibody, has been widely used off-label to treat individuals with hemophilia who develop inhibitors. However, its efficacy and safety in this context have not been thoroughly evaluated. This review aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of rituximab for treating inhibitors in people with severe inherited hemophilia A or B. To conduct this review, researchers searched the Cochrane Cystic Fibrosis and Genetic Disorders Group's Coagulopathies Trials Register, which includes data from electronic databases, hand-searched journals, and conference abstracts. They also reviewed reference lists of relevant articles and conducted additional searches in bibliographic databases and trial registries. The most recent search of the Coagulopathies Trials Register was performed on March 19, 2020. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and controlled clinical trials that investigated the efficacy and safety of rituximab in treating inhibitors in individuals with hemophilia. However, no studies meeting these criteria were identified. As a result, no RCTs were included in the analysis. The authors concluded that there is currently no high-quality evidence from randomized controlled trials regarding the efficacy and safety of rituximab for treating inhibitors in people with hemophilia. The available evidence is limited to case reports and case series. To establish the role of rituximab in this context, well-designed randomized controlled trials are urgently needed. In the interim, meta-analyses of existing case reports and case series may provide some preliminary insights into its potential benefits and risks.
